# `get_controls`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

List the camera controls with their limits and read-only flags.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb41d0, GetControls @0x11d720, camera GetControls @0x1537d0, OpenCamera table build @0x1526f0 (64-bit build); 32-bit GetControls @0xabf1c, OpenCamera @0xdaeb0; camera library control caps from its debug information |

Returns a copy of the device's control table under the camera lock. Requires an open camera. The table is the device's own, built when the camera opens, with imager control ids 0, 1, 4, 19, 20, 23, 24 and 25 always and 5, 6, 7, 8 and 22 on cooled cameras (22 on the 64-bit build only); see the result schema and the spec (READ). Limits are fixed in the firmware except the maximum gain and, on the 64-bit build, the maximum exposure, which come from the camera at open; their per-camera values are unresolved on the 64-bit build. The 32-bit build fixes Exposure at 30..2000000000 and its compiled-in camera library sets the Gain maximum to 400 (600 for the secondary camera on the S30 Pro and S50 Pro branches) (READ). A client SHOULD use this reply, not an assumed static range, to learn the limits for set_control_value. Units (READ, camera library, except exposure) are exposure microseconds (INFERRED); gain tenths of a dB on multiplicative-gain sensors, raw analogue gain otherwise; target temperature degrees C, clamped to -40..30; cooler power percent; cooler on boolean; red/blue white balance gain with 100 as unity, affecting only pixel format 3.

Side effects: None beyond taking the camera lock to copy the map; no shared state is written.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_controls"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 318 | Camera absent, closed, or camera id negative | `device not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No parameter errors. The 64-bit build's camera-supplied maximum gain and exposure are unresolved per camera; read them from this reply.

## Example

Request, list:

```json
{"id":40,"method":"get_controls"}
```

Reply, ok - Shape and names READ; Gain and Exposure maxima invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_controls","result":[{"name":"Gain","min":0,"max":300,"read_only":false},{"name":"Exposure","min":30,"max":2000000000,"read_only":false},{"name":"Temperature","min":30,"max":2000000000,"read_only":true}],"code":0,"id":40}
```

Reply, closed:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_controls","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":41}
```
